question: What is a rectovaginal fistula?

options.A: A congenital narrowing of the lower vaginal canal
options.B: A tear in the perineal skin reaching the anus
options.C: An abnormal tract connecting the rectum and vagina
options.D: An infection of the Bartholin's gland in the vulva

explanation: A rectovaginal fistula creates an unwanted passage between the rectal wall and the vaginal wall, leading to the leakage of stool or gas through the vagina. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T13#GNS216_U5_T13_h1)

question: Why does a rectovaginal fistula cause psychological distress for patients?

options.A: Sudden and permanent loss of all lower limb mobility
options.B: Involuntary passage of flatus and feces through the vagina
options.C: Complete inability to ever conceive biological children again
options.D: Severe chronic pain located exclusively in the upper abdomen

explanation: The uncontrolled leakage of bowel contents via the vaginal opening causes profound hygiene challenges and social embarrassment. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T13#GNS216_U5_T13_h1)

question: The primary cause of rectovaginal fistulas in Nigeria is:

options.A: Chronic pelvic inflammatory disease caused by STIs
options.B: Obstetric trauma from prolonged obstructed labor
options.C: Congenital malformations present from early childhood
options.D: Routine use of midline episiotomies by midwives

explanation: Unrelieved obstructed labor compresses the vaginal and rectal tissues, leading to tissue death and subsequent fistula formation. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T13#GNS216_U5_T13_h2)

question: How does ischemia contribute to fistula formation during difficult labor?

options.A: Infected amniotic fluid eats away at the vaginal mucosa
options.B: Hormonal imbalances prevent normal postpartum tissue healing
options.C: Compressed blood supply causes localized tissue death and breakdown
options.D: Extreme physical stretching instantly tears the muscle fibers apart

explanation: Pressure from the baby's head cuts off oxygen supply to the septum, resulting in necrosis and an opening between the organs. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T13#GNS216_U5_T13_h2)

question: What is the classic symptom reported by a patient with a rectovaginal fistula?

options.A: Passage of feces and flatus through the vagina
options.B: Bright red bleeding from the urethra during urination
options.C: Severe sharp pain during the start of menstruation
options.D: Inability to control the flow of urine while coughing

explanation: The defining clinical feature is the escape of bowel contents through the vaginal canal due to the abnormal tract. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T13#GNS216_U5_T13_h3)

question: A patient complains of recurrent foul-smelling vaginal discharge and passing gas vaginally after a difficult delivery. What condition should you suspect first?
explanation: These classic symptoms point directly to an abnormal connection between the bowel and the reproductive tract following childbirth. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T13#GNS216_U5_T13_h3)

question: What bedside test uses a colored dye in the rectum to confirm a rectovaginal fistula?
explanation: Instilling methylene blue into the rectum and checking for blue stains on a vaginal gauze confirms the presence of a tract. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T13#GNS216_U5_T13_h4)

question: Why is an examination under anesthesia (EUA) often performed before scheduling fistula surgery?

options.A: To clean out impacted stool from the large intestine prior to surgery
options.B: To immediately close the opening while the patient is fully unconscious
options.C: To prevent the development of a postoperative wound infection
options.D: To accurately assess tissue quality and exact fistula location without patient pain

explanation: Relaxed pelvic muscles under anesthesia allow the clinician to thoroughly evaluate the defect and plan the appropriate surgical approach. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T13#GNS216_U5_T13_h4)

question: The primary goal of bowel preparation before rectovaginal fistula surgery is to:

options.A: Prevent the formation of deep vein thrombosis
options.B: Stimulate rapid weight gain before the operation
options.C: Minimize fecal contamination of the surgical site
options.D: Diagnose the exact cause of the original tear

explanation: Clearing the bowel reduces stool load and lowers the risk of wound infection and repair breakdown. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T13#GNS216_U5_T13_h5)

question: Why is nutritional optimization a key component of preoperative care for these patients?

options.A: High-fiber diets eliminate the need for mechanical enemas
options.B: Full nutrient stores prevent the need for general anesthesia
options.C: Good nutrition stops the fistula tract from growing larger
options.D: Adequate protein and vitamins promote optimal wound healing

explanation: Surgical repair of ischemic or damaged tissue requires proper cellular nutrition to ensure the tissues successfully knit together. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T13#GNS216_U5_T13_h5)

question: When is a temporary colostomy most likely created during rectovaginal fistula management?

options.A: For every single routine primary transvaginal repair
options.B: As a permanent replacement for normal bowel function
options.C: Only when the patient refuses to take oral antibiotics
options.D: In complex, recurrent, or badly damaged fistula cases

explanation: Diverting stool protects delicate or complicated surgical repairs from fecal contamination while healing takes place. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T13#GNS216_U5_T13_h6)

question: What is the main purpose of using a tissue flap during a rectovaginal fistula repair?

options.A: To permanently block the normal passage of urine
options.B: To stretch the vaginal canal to a larger diameter
options.C: To cover the defect with well-vascularized, healthy tissue
options.D: To completely eliminate the need for postoperative antibiotics

explanation: Bringing fresh, good-blood-supply tissue over the repaired area greatly improves the chances of successful tissue fusion. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T13#GNS216_U5_T13_h6)

question: Why are stool softeners commonly prescribed after rectovaginal fistula repair?

options.A: To completely stop bowel function for several weeks
options.B: To speed up the total digestion time of all food eaten
options.C: To cure any lingering urinary tract infections quickly
options.D: To prevent straining and protect the suture line from pressure

explanation: Soft stools pass easily without requiring hard pushing, which prevents the fresh stitches from tearing apart. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T13#GNS216_U5_T13_h7)

question: What is a key nursing intervention regarding bladder management post-surgery?

options.A: Removing all fluid intake to keep the surgical dressings dry
options.B: Checking urine specific gravity every thirty minutes around the clock
options.C: Maintaining an indwelling urinary catheter to prevent bladder distension
options.D: Encouraging heavy physical exercise to stimulate normal voiding reflexes

explanation: A distended bladder pushes against the anterior vaginal wall, placing unwanted mechanical stress on the healing surgical repair. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T13#GNS216_U5_T13_h7)

question: The most common and challenging complication after a rectovaginal fistula repair is:

options.A: Permanent total paralysis of both lower limbs
options.B: Complete loss of kidney function requiring dialysis
options.C: Sudden spontaneous rupture of the uterine wall
options.D: Fistula recurrence and failure of the repair

explanation: Due to tension, infection, or poor tissue quality, some repairs fail to heal, resulting in the return of the fistula tract. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T13#GNS216_U5_T13_h8)

question: What can cause vaginal or rectal strictures following fistula surgery?

options.A: Excessive scar tissue formation during the healing process
options.B: Consuming a high-fiber diet too early in recovery
options.C: Failure to administer high doses of intravenous fluids
options.D: Leaving the indwelling urinary catheter in place too long

explanation: Fibrous scar tissue can contract and narrow the lumen of the vagina or rectum, leading to strictures. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T13#GNS216_U5_T13_h8)
